news.quote: Danaos Corp (DAC) posted $8.32 in adjusted earnings per share as dry bulk revenue surged 69% and the container fleet reached 99.6% utilization.

touches.claim: Operating income declined from 580,661 in 2023 to 540,884 in 2024 and 498,766 in 2025 (table in thousands), while container segment revenues fell 1.6% from $475.6 million in 2025 to $468.2 million in 2026 and investment results swung from (25,179) in 2024 to 29,541 in 2025.
Danaos achieved 98.2% containership utilization in 2025 (with 44 unscheduled off-hire days) and 97.7% in the three months ended June 30, 2026, supported by Danaos Shipping's operational management.

Operating revenues grew from $ 973,583 (table in thousands) in 2023 to $ 1,042,456 (table in thousands) in 2025 while generating 498,766 (table in thousands) in operating income and holding $ 1,037,292 (table in thousands) in cash against 1,318,353 (table in thousands) in total liabilities.

Containership fleet expansion is a primary growth driver, with 35 newbuilding containerships (232,948 TEU; $2.7 billion purchase price) ordered since 2022 and 27 under-construction containerships (174,550 TEUs) scheduled for delivery in 2026 through 2029, while newbuilding additions increased container revenue by $3.2 million in the three months ended June 30, 2026.

Drybulk fleet expansion and higher charter rates are a major current growth driver, with average drybulk vessels rising from 1.1 in 2023 to 10.0 in 2025 and 11.0 in the three months ended June 30, 2026, alongside Newcastlemax newbuildings (approximately 844,000 DWT; $297.3 million) scheduled for 2028, driving a 57.3% ($13.0 million) drybulk revenue increase to $35.7 million in that period.

For drybulk growth to continue, Time Charter Equivalent rates ($30,401 per day in the three months ended June 30, 2026 vs. $17,934 per day a year earlier) and fleet utilization (98% in 2025; 99.5% in the three months ended June 30, 2026) must remain supportive, and the 2028 Newcastlemax deliveries must proceed.

news.why: Danaos beat Q3 2026 expectations with revenue up 7.9% to $284.3 million, adjusted EPS of $8.32, 99.6% containership utilization, and a 69% surge in dry bulk revenue, reversing prior revenue and profit declines.
